chart_explainers.body: Cost charts explain fees, spread, slippage, latency, impact, opportunity cost, and missing provider evidence.
Quantum/classical charts show structural readiness and classical fallback routes. They do not claim quantum advantage.
Charts show what a provider route will explain after receipts exist; no fake values are rendered.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Profit and loss. In this dashboard it appears only after receipts exist.
glossary.why_it_matters: Shows whether a completed path gained or lost value after costs.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Estimated cash result after costs and constraints, when evidence exists.
glossary.why_it_matters: Keeps QTT from ranking gross edge while hiding costs.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Transaction cost analysis: fees, spread, slippage, latency, impact, and opportunity cost.
glossary.why_it_matters: Costs can turn an apparent edge into no-trade.

glossary.plain_english_definition: The gap between buy and sell prices.
glossary.why_it_matters: A wider spread makes entry and exit more expensive.

glossary.plain_english_definition: The difference between expected and actual execution price.
glossary.why_it_matters: Slippage can erase expected edge.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Value lost because a signal or order arrives late.
glossary.why_it_matters: Late execution can change fill quality.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Price movement caused by trying to trade size.
glossary.why_it_matters: Large size can worsen execution.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Value lost by locking capital in one path instead of another.
glossary.why_it_matters: Capital has competing uses.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Likelihood an order fills under the planned terms.
glossary.why_it_matters: Low fill probability reduces usable expected value.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Only part of the intended order fills.
glossary.why_it_matters: Partial fills can leave unwanted exposure.

glossary.plain_english_definition: How much size a strategy can handle before quality degrades.
glossary.why_it_matters: Capacity limits prevent oversizing.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Many traders using similar signals or routes.
glossary.why_it_matters: Crowding can reduce edge and increase costs.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A first-class comparator that may beat available trade candidates.
glossary.why_it_matters: No-trade prevents forcing weak trades.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A best current candidate compared with alternatives.
glossary.why_it_matters: Keeps QTT from assuming the first candidate is best.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A conservative estimate under uncertainty.
glossary.why_it_matters: Protects against overconfident estimates.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A check for patterns that may be statistical noise.
glossary.why_it_matters: Reduces overfit risk.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A strategy that looks good on old data but may fail later.
glossary.why_it_matters: Overfit candidates need more evidence.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Portfolio benefit after diversification and capital cost.
glossary.why_it_matters: A trade can be good alone but bad for the portfolio.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Similar-regime prior evidence, not current proof.
glossary.why_it_matters: Memory speeds review but does not prove profit.

glossary.plain_english_definition: An immutable QTT knowledge object.
glossary.why_it_matters: QTT optimizes trade plans, not QKUs.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A set of immutable formulas used to evaluate a candidate.
glossary.why_it_matters: Stacks need computability and route evidence.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Whether a problem is structurally mappable to quantum forms.
glossary.why_it_matters: This is not a quantum advantage claim.

glossary.plain_english_definition: The non-quantum comparator route.
glossary.why_it_matters: QTT must keep a strong classical baseline.

glossary.plain_english_definition: The governed downstream component that may release live venue orders later.
glossary.why_it_matters: The dashboard does not release orders.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A tightly gated small live review stage later in the launch path.
glossary.why_it_matters: It requires downstream evidence and approval.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A non-live test path using paper execution receipts later.
glossary.why_it_matters: R2 only previews the request route.

glossary.plain_english_definition: A historical scenario test path later.
glossary.why_it_matters: R2 only previews the request route.

glossary.plain_english_definition: Observation beside live conditions without direct live execution authority.
glossary.why_it_matters: R2 only shows contract routes.

Paste or type trade idea in normal English.
Choose objective: maximize expected net cash, preserve capital, minimize drawdown, improve diversification, test quantum/classical stack, or let QTT decide using default policy.
